item.content:
Introduction

Quantization, in deep learning is a lossy compression process of mapping weights of a neural network model from real values to fixed bit-width integers.

The process of quantization, can be effectively applied either while training a network or post training the network - depending on the input data distribution within a dataset and the kernels distribution within the network. The mapping constraints a network however, for a chosen bit-width of integers while yielding an affordable accuracy drop in the model’s performance.

Quantization, improves memory footprint of a model; specifically, in resource constrained devices. In tailored hardwares - consisting of Accelerators or CPUs supporting SIMD quantization can help in vectorization of weights (learnt parameters) and activations (intermediate computations between layers of a network) in accordance with the core-matrix multiplier register arrays of the hardware; thereby, increasing the inference speed of a model significantly.

Formulation

Mathematically, the weights of a kernel undergoes transformation from $\mathbb{R}$ domain to $\mathbb{Z}$ as,

$$ \{ x \ \epsilon \ \mathbb{R} \ | \ \alpha \leq x \leq \beta\ \} \ \mapsto \{ x_q \ \epsilon \ \mathbb{Z} \ | \ \alpha_q \leq x_q \leq \beta_q \ \} $$

The range of the integer values are decided by $b$-bits of integer representation chosen for mapping $x \ \mapsto x_q$.

For example, if the range of $x$ is $[-8.05, 8.08]$ - by choosing $b=8$, the quantized space will have $2^b=2^8=256$ values. The quantized space can be uniformly or non-uniformly spread across the ranges where only integers can exist between $[-128, 127]$. For instance, in an uniform distribution $\forall x$ each $x$ will be mapped to a nearby integer value $x_q$ representing a constant scale of $(-8.0 + x_q * (1/256))$ in the original domain.

We will see in the later section, distinct approaches of achieving the scaling factor of the quantization process. For most of the practical cases in edge computing, the uniform (or linear) integer mapping is far than enough to represent a mathematical approximation to which an outcome belongs to (an example can be classification problem).

Transformations

Theoretically, the weights can be mapped from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ either by,

  • Linear spacing (uniform): Quantized values are equally spaced in the original $\mathbb{R}$ domain and mapped linearly
  • Non-Linear spacing (non-uniform): A careful mapping of the $\mathbb{R}$ values depending on the part of the data that often occurs frequently but has data at larger extremes as well. The scaling depends on the position at which the bit value is represented at

Linear Transformation

Let us consider linear scaling for the transformation and define the quantization process as: $$ \begin{equation} x_q = round(x/s - b) \tag{1} \label{eq:quantization} \end{equation} $$
achieves the integer mapping. Note that, the ‘round off’ introduces noise into the conversion.

Later, to rescale the data into a real value, de-quantization process will be applied through: $$ \begin{equation} x = s(x_q + b) \tag{2} \label{eq:dequantization} \end{equation} $$

When $x$ is at $\alpha$ the scaling imposes $\alpha_q$ after transformation. Similarly, $\beta_q$ will be the final outcome when $x$ reaches $\beta$. In reference to equation (\ref{eq:quantization}), we can confide the values of $s$ and $b$ by formulating a linear systems of equation$^1$ as we are trying to solve for $s$ and $b$ that imposes the minima and maxima of the transformation, $$ \begin{equation} \alpha=s(\alpha_q + b) \tag{3} \label{eq:alpha scaling} \end{equation} $$

$$ \begin{equation} \beta=s(\beta_q + b) \tag{4} \label{eq:beta scaling} \end{equation} $$

To solve for $b$, we can rearrange $s$ in the equation (\ref{eq:alpha scaling}) to be

$$ \begin{equation} s=(\alpha / (\alpha_q + b)) \tag{1a} \label{eq:alpha scaling rearrangement} \end{equation} $$

substituting equation (\ref{eq:alpha scaling rearrangement}) in equation (\ref{eq:beta scaling}) we get,

$$ \begin{equation} \beta = {(\alpha \beta_q + \alpha b) \over (\alpha_q + b)} \tag{4a} \end{equation} $$

$$ \begin{equation} \alpha \beta_q - \beta \alpha_q + b (\alpha - \beta) = 0 \tag{4b} \end{equation} $$

$$ \begin{equation} b = {(\alpha \beta_q - \beta \alpha_q) \over (\beta - \alpha)} \tag{4c} \label{eq:unrounded zero point} \end{equation} $$

Technically, equation (\ref{eq:unrounded zero point}) cannot be a fractional number. It is the zero-point or the base point from which the scaled numbers are distributed. This could be derived by keeping $x=0$ in equation (\ref{eq:quantization}), resulting in mapped $x_q = round(-b)$. Therefore we must impose,

$$ \begin{equation} \boxed{z = -round({(\alpha \beta_q - \beta \alpha_q) \over (\beta - \alpha)})} \tag{5} \label{eq:zero point} \end{equation} $$

and substituting $b$ from equation (\ref{eq:unrounded zero point}) in equation (\ref{eq:alpha scaling}) we can simplify the equation in terms of $s$ as,

$$ \begin{equation} \beta = {s (\beta_q (\beta - \alpha) + \alpha \beta_q - \beta \alpha_q) \over (\beta - \alpha)} \tag{3a} \end{equation} $$

$$ \begin{equation} s = {\beta (\beta - \alpha) \over \beta_q (\beta - \alpha) + \alpha \beta_q - \beta \alpha_q}\tag{3b} \end{equation} $$

$$ \begin{equation} \boxed{s = {(\beta - \alpha) \over (\beta_q - \alpha_q)}} \tag{6} \end{equation} $$

We can finally redefine the quantization transformation process from equation (\ref{eq:quantization}) to $$ \begin{equation} x_q = round((x/s) + z) \end{equation} $$

where the mapping constraint must be $\{ \alpha_q <= x_q <= \beta_q \}$ and the values needs to be clipped off if they are beyond the boundary i.e., $$ \begin{equation} \boxed{x_q = clip(round((x/s) + z), \alpha_q, \beta_q)} \tag{7} \label{eq:final quantization} \end{equation} $$

The de-quantization transformation process from equation (\ref{eq:dequantization}) can then be defined as,

$$ \begin{equation} \boxed{x = s (x_q - z)} \tag{8} \label{eq:final dequantization} \end{equation} $$

Non-Linear Transformation

A non-uniform transformation extends the linear transformation merely by two additional steps,

  1. By compressing the weights of a kernel with a non-linear function and then linear transforming the data
  2. At inference, by decompressing the quantized data - while computing the intermediates of the forward pass

We can mathematically formulate these steps by extending the equation (\ref{eq:final quantization}) to define quantization process as:

$$ \begin{equation} \boxed{x_q = clip(({round(f(x) * \lambda) \over s}) + z), \alpha_q, \beta_q)} \tag{9} \label{eq:final non-linear quantization} \end{equation} $$

Note that, $\forall x$ the $\lambda$ in equation (\ref{eq:final non-linear quantization}) controls the squashing factor of the near by values. The choice of $\lambda$ is optional but depends upon the compression function that is applied. The $\lambda$ often is the resolution dial of the overall compression function and will be within the space $\{ \alpha < \lambda < \beta \}$.

The dequantization process however running at the inference, has to decompress the data with an exact inverse function of the equation (\ref{eq:final non-linear quantization}) as,

$$ \begin{equation} \boxed{x = s (({f^{-1}(x_q) \over \lambda}) - z)} \tag{10} \label{eq: final non-linear dequantization} \end{equation} $$

The functions $f(x)$ and $f^{-1}(x_q)$ are to be chosen carefully depending on the architecture and the kernel distribution of the network, however the squashing factor $\lambda$ will be a parameter learnt while training the network or post training - for a chosen (de-)compression function.

In deep learning, often the kernel appears to have Gaussian distribution with few outliers. Lets consider, arcsinh a specialized non-linear function often used in LLMs to compress 16-bit float to 4-bit integers!

References

  1. Leo MAO’s Log Book - Quantization for Neural Networks
  2. Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference

item.title: ಪಾಶ
item.description:
ತರುಲತೆಗಳದರಿದವು ರೆಕ್ಕೆಗಳ ಬಡಿತಕ್ಕೆ,
ಚಡಪಡಿಸುವ ಚಿಟ್ಟೆಗಳ ವರ್ಣ ಝೇಂಕಾರವನರಿತು
ಹೂ ಪಟಲಗಳುದರಿದವು ಹೊಸ ಕುಸುಮವ ಬಯಸಿ,
ಕನಸಿನ ಮೂಡಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಚದರಿತ್ತು ಸೂರ್ಯ ರಶ್ಮಿ

ಹರಡಿದ ತರಗೆಲೆಗಳ ಮಧ್ಯೆ, ನಿನ್ನ ದಾರಿಯನರಸಿ,
ಗುರುತಿರದ ಹೆಜ್ಜೆಗಳ ಹುಡುಕುವ ತಿರುಕ ನಾನು
ನಸುಕಿನ ಹನಿಗಳ ಕಾತೊರೆದು ಕೂಡಿಡುವ, ಚಿಗುರೆಲೆಗಳ ಕೇಳಲೆ?
ಅವಳ ಸನಿಹವೇ ಬಯಸುವ ಪಾಶವಾವುದು?

item.title: ಗಾಳಿಪಟ
item.description:
ನೀಲ ಗಗನದಂಚು ತೊರೆದು, ಸಾಲು ಮೋಡ ಸರಿದು ಸೆಳೆದು,
ಸರಿಸಿ ಸಾಗುತಿತ್ತು ನಭದಿ ಕೇಸರೀಯ ಪಥ
ತಿಳಿಯ ಗಾಳಿ ತಂಪು ತಳಿದು, ಹಗಲ ಸಮಯದಂಚು ಹರಿದು,
ಚುಕ್ಕಿ ಚಂದ್ರರನ್ನು ತರುತಲಿತ್ತು ಕಾಲರಥ

ಹರಿದ ಅಂಗಿ, ಬಿರಿದ ಚಡ್ಡಿ, ಧೂಳು ಬರಿದ ಕಾಲ್ಗಳು
ಪಟದ ಸೂತ್ರ ಬಿಗಿದು ಎಳೆದು ಸುತ್ತುತಿರುವ ಕೈಗಳು
ಉಗ್ಗು ಬಾಯಿ ಸುಗ್ಗಿ ಸಿಹಿಯ ನೆವರುತಿರುವ ನಾಲಗೆ
ಓರೆ ತಲೆಯ ಸರಿಸಿ ಮೇಲೆ ಹುಡುಕುತಿರುವ ತೊಪ್ಪಿಗೆ

ಒಣಕು ಟೊಂಗೆ ಕಡ್ಡಿ ಪಡಿಕೆ, ಹಸಿರು ನೀಲ ಹಾಳೆ ಪಲಕ
ರಂಗು ರಂಗು ಚಿಟ್ಟೆೆ ಸರಣಿ, ಸಾಲು ಹೂವು ಎದರು ಬದಿಗೆ
ಕೆಂಪು ಸೂತ್ರ ಮಧ್ಯೆಯಿಂದ, ಕೋಣೆಗಳನು ಭದ್ರ ಮಾಡಿ
ಸೀಳು ಕಾಗದಕ್ಕೆ ಬಿಗಿದ ಸಾಲು ತಳಿರ ಬಾಲಂಗೋಚಿ

ಹರಡಿ ತನ್ನ ಬೀಸು ಬಾಲ, ಸಂಜೆ ಸೂಸು ಗಾಳಿಯೆಡೆಗೆ
ಪಟವು ತೇಲುತಿತ್ತು ಸಡಿಲ ದಾರದಿಂದೆತ್ತರೆತ್ತರ
ಸೂತ್ರವೆಣೆದ ಹಕ್ಕಿಯಂತೆ, ಗಗನ ರಾಯಭಾರಿಯಾಗಿ,
ಮಿನುಗು ಚುಕ್ಕಿ ಚುಂಬಿಸುತ್ತ, ತರುತ ಭುವಿಗೆ ಹರುಷ

ತರಣಿ ತನ್ನ ಮನೆಗೆ ತೆರಳಿ, ಸಂಜೆ ಸಾಗಿ ಸೊರಗುತಿತ್ತು,
ಹೊತ್ತು ಮಿರುತಿದ್ದರೂನು ತೀರುತಿಲ್ಲ ಪಟದ ಬಯಕೆ
ಪಟದ ಹಿಂದೆ ತೇಲುವಾಸೆ, ಜಿಗಿದರೆಷ್ಟು ತೇಲೆನು
ಸೂತ್ರ ಹಿಡಿದು ಓಡುತಿರುವೆ ಪಟದ ವೇಗ ಮೀರೆನು

item.title: ಚೈತ್ರ
item.description:
ಹಳೆಗನಸು, ಹಳೆಸಮರ, ಅಚಲ ಛಲಕ್ಕೆಲ್ಲಿದೆ ಹೊಸ ಚಿಗುರುಗಳ ಪರಿಚಯ?
ಬೇರುಗಳು ನುರಿತಿಹುವು ಹಲವು ಚೈತ್ರಗಳ ಉತ್ಸಾಹವನರಿತು,
ಹಳೆಯ ತೊಡುಗೆಯ ಕಳಚಿ ಕಾದಿಹವು ಹೊಸಯತ್ನಕೆ!

ಹೊಸತನಕೆ ಹೆಸರಿಟ್ಟವರನು ಮರೆತು, ಹೊಸತನವ ವರ್ಗಾಯಿಸಿ,
ಹಸಿರು-ಹೊಂಬಾಳೆ ತಂದಿಹುದು ಹೊಸ ವರುಷ!
ಇರಲಿ ಸಾಧನೆಗಿಷ್ಟು ಕಹಿ ಬೇವು, ಮರಳಿ ನಗಲೊಂದಿಷ್ಟು ಬೆಲ್ಲ,
ಅಳತೆ ಸಮವಿರಲಿ ಅನನ್ಯ ವೈಖರಿಗಳಿಗಾಗಿ.
ಎಣೆಬಿಡದೆ ಸರಿಸಾಗಲಿ ಸಮರ ಹೊಸ ವರುಷಗಳಿಗಾಗಿ.

item.title: ಮಳೆ
item.description:
ಜಿಟಿ ಮಳೆಗೆಲ್ಲಿದೆ, ಪಯಣಿಗನ ಕಾಳಜಿ?

ತೊರೆವವನು ದೂರುವನು, ತೊರೆದವನು ಮೀಗುವನು
ಮಳೆಗೆಲ್ಲಿದೆ ಅದರ ಪರಿವು?
ಹರುಷವ ಪಸರಿಸುವ ಹೂವುಗಳು ಹೇಳುವವು, ಹನಿಗಳ ಸಿಹಿ ವಿತರಣವ,
ಕಿರಣಗಳ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲನಗಳಿಂದ.

ಪ್ರೇಯಸಿಯ ಮುನಿಸಿನ ನಗುವಿಗೋ,
ಭಕ್ತಿಯ ಪರಾಕಾಷ್ಠೆಗೋ,
ಚಿತೆಯ ಆಲಂಕಾರಗಳಿಗೋ,
ಎಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರುವಮೋ ಅಲ್ಲಿ ತೋರುವವು ಮಳೆಯ ಕಾಯಕವನ್ನ.

item.title: First Post. Writing - in the era of AI?
item.description:
Why blogging?

Clearly, this is an era of AI that we are witnessing. With LLMs simulating & mocking human intelligence, conventional world is merely depicting a portal to a dystopian era. Agents are solving - text translation, text interpretation and text transformation in seconds that were once considered unsolvable by humans due to the heterogeneity in the language space. But today, for an average Joe, building UI rich websites (vibe coding), performing data analysis on their spending & investments (Gemini) are been tailored to executable scripts in seconds by commencing a computer with natural languages!
item.content:
Why blogging?

Clearly, this is an era of AI that we are witnessing. With LLMs simulating & mocking human intelligence, conventional world is merely depicting a portal to a dystopian era. Agents are solving - text translation, text interpretation and text transformation in seconds that were once considered unsolvable by humans due to the heterogeneity in the language space. But today, for an average Joe, building UI rich websites (vibe coding), performing data analysis on their spending & investments (Gemini) are been tailored to executable scripts in seconds by commencing a computer with natural languages!

Stack overflow is hitting all time low in their listings for any technical assistance post while LLMs are conjugating as senators - from code explanations to code reviews.

Their performance is a topic for another day but in this era of “Ask Chat-GPT to create a concrete plan for 3 days road trip in Switzerland”, who has overcome their ADHD to read a blog post?

Well, I don’t intend to address the blog to anyone to be honest, it’s a note keeper for me; a salient friend who wires up a few neurons to organize some of my thoughts and pen them down here or to experiment with Feynman’s technique for a concept that I’m trying to understand or to avoid brain rot from information overflow, scrolling over the social media postings; I will be writing or we may all have to - at some point in the future we won’t need to be coding anyways!

What’s on my mind?

At times, I will write technical contents - Math behind Deep Learning architectures, intrinsics of C++ and exemplary usages of certain software frameworks for developers. I’m an advocate of philosophy - Vedanta has impeccable sources of wisdom to ponder and large verses to explain; I will try to carefully decipher the contextual translations of the verses in a comprehensible manner; and in ಕನ್ನಡ, some of my poems and short stories will be constantly posted.

Who ought to be the listeners?

The universe and serendipity. One who pops up for a reference, one who wants to discuss further on a post and for those of you who wants to fix typos or equations in my articles - all are welcome to visit this site!
